lob_descriptions.Finance: Financial accounting, controlling, treasury, and reporting data products from SAP S/4HANA Cloud. Covers Record-to-Report and Procure-to-Pay with master data for cost centers, profit centers, G/L accounts, and journal entries.

lob_descriptions.Unclassified: Human Capital Management data products from SAP SuccessFactors plus cross-functional master data. Includes talent management, recruiting analytics, compensation, employee profiles, and extensibility objects.

products.description: A general ledger account represents G/L Account Master Data in the Chart of Accounts area which contain information about the G/L account that are valid for all company codes. The chart of accounts area also contains data that control how a G/L account is created in the company code-specific area. Examples: (1) Information if the G/L Account is a Profit & Loss Account (2) Description of the G/L Account **Business Context**: General Ledger Account is concerned with processing and reporting all postings relevant to external financial accounting. Due to the nature of the Universal Journal, the process also includes elements of internal accounting (Controlling). As part of these activities, General Ledger Account line items are processed, which potentially contains personal data. The DP is intended to be used for financial accounting, ensuring accurate, auditable, and compliant financial reporting.

products.description: A billing document is a set of data that can represent a customer invoice, credit memo, debit memo, pro forma invoice, or the corresponding cancellation document. Every billing document consists of a header and a number of items. The header contains data that applies to the entire document, while items contain data that is only valid for the respective item. Most billing documents are posted to financial accounting to create the required journal entries for the relevant accounts (for example, accounts receivable). The most common type of billing document is the customer invoice, which you use to request payment from customers for products you have supplied or services you have rendered. Similarly, you can use credit memos to credit customers when you owe them money, as in the case of customer returns. **Business Context**: The data product potentially contains personal data that is intended to be used for customer billing and invoice management.

products.description: A consolidation version is a distinct version of data in consolidation. In addition to a consolidation version for actual data, other versions of data that can be managed in parallel can be created, so that alternative results for the purposes of simulation, planning, and restatement can be produced. A consolidation version can be used for parallel processing with different data categories, accounting principles, and valuations, such as multiple group currencies. To each consolidation version, special versions are assigned. The assignment of special versions enables the reuse of the maintained settings of a special version among different consolidation versions: The control parameters are entered only once in a special version and these settings are then reflected in all the consolidation versions to which the special version is assigned. Examples for special versions are data entry, consolidation unit attributes, financial statement item attributes, group structure, exchange rates, reclassification and elimination. **Business Context**:
products.industries: High Tech,Mill Products,Industrial Machinery and Components,Retail

The data product also includes the absence type, which is a logical grouping of absence requests. It is used to specify the group characteristics, for example, whether an absence request represents a vacation or sick leave. It also restricts the allowed values for attributes of the absence request.
